done.why: I got the pearls early, then lost the thread in the glass maze of oddly-angled rooms and the ice puzzle. I couldn't tell which moves counted.

about: A Zork II style underground empire. A wizard has hoarded the Empire's lost treasures south of a ravine. You solve a riddle door, cross a spinning carousel room, and meet a dragon, an ice wall and a glass maze.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared and hinted at where the treasure was, including the stone door and the room that won't keep still.
Taking the Wizard's illusory sphere got a wry refusal: the room 'has the grace to look embarrassed'.
The carousel moved me straight into the riddle room. Answering 'well' opened the door.
The ice mass cannot be burned with a matchbook, and I found nothing else to melt it.
The window in the glass maze flickers by some hidden count, and I couldn't tell which moves feed it.

wished: A clearer hint about how to melt the ice
A way to stop the carousel
A clue to what the maze window counts

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It gave me a goal and a route.

lines.line: The room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: A witty way to handle illusory objects.

fun.why: Good early momentum, then I hit an opaque maze.

engagement.why: The goal was clear at first and then fuzzy.

difficulty.why: The ice and the maze gave me no feedback I could use.

interestingness.why: The Zork II setting is re-imagined with new illusions and a carousel.

prose.why: Dry, witty narration, especially around the illusions and the carousel.
